title: Validation of a novel pre-test concept (DrugAsens®) by quantification of THC concentrations in saliva
summary:
As part of the increasing legalisation of cannabis products, the limit value for delta9-THC in blood serum, which applies to drivers in road traffic in accordance with Section 24a StVG, was raised from 1.0 ng/ml to 3.5 ng/ml in August 2024. From a legal point of view, the increase in the limit value now poses the following problem: during traffic controls, immunochemical urine or saliva rapid tests are used to pre-select alleged drug offenders, but in their current form they are likely to be too sensitive to optimally reflect the new (higher) limit value. 
This threatens a large number of ultimately unnecessary interventions in the personal rights and physical integrity of road users as well as an overload of police and downstream agencies (judiciary, driving licence authorities, etc.) in road safety work.
Innovative testing principles such as the technical sensor of the DrugAsens® can lead to improved drug detection in road traffic, but their reliability must be tested before routine use.
conditions: Regular cannabis users consume once under supervision with saliva samples taken

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Anamnestically healthy, adult, cannabis-accustomed (i.e. cannabis use at least once a month) women and men of all ages and constitutional types. Regular cannabis use can be expressly accepted.
Exclusion criteria:
- Minors
- Pre-existing cardiac and/or psychiatric conditions*
- Pregnancy or breastfeeding*
- First-time cannabis users*
- Desired consumption of >500 mg cannabis per joint under study conditions 
- noticeable substance influence due to the consumption of (other) drugs/medication/alcohol on the day of the trial
- Multiple use of cannabis during the study day

*With regard to cannabis experience/pre-existing conditions/pregnancy, the selection procedure is based on the subjects' self-reporting, as the completely anonymous study design means that no personal/clinical anamnesis can be collected.
